Kumarkand (F30)

Region (English scoring-table region): Bulwar.

In a sentence: A Bulwari human state held beneath the Sun Elves, conspiring for independence and relying on Sunriders and mercenaries to revive an ancient empire—before having to defend its coast.

Narrative: High | Mission-tree length: Long (52 F30-related mission definitions, including phase conditions) | Verified version: local Mod supports EU4 v1.37.5.0 | Distinctiveness: High | Degree of confinement: Medium-high (starting as a subject and facing a later crisis) | Early pressure: High | Expansion capacity: High

A Subject's Conspiracy

Unlike a formable, Kumarkand (F30) already exists in 1444. It is a Zanite human monarchy in the Suran region, follows the New Sun Cult, and has Sun Elf as an accepted culture. Its opening ruler is Serakh II of the Remmanu dynasty, with Saed as heir. Current mission text and the official development diary both place it under the overlordship of Varamhar, a Sun Elf state, and involve it in the Whispering Shadows incident. The court, nobles, merchants, and neighboring states appear to conduct ordinary affairs; in secret, however, they are plotting against their overlord. The opening tension is more than “a weak country fighting an independence war”: amid suspicion, potential allies, and religious politics, you must decide whom to trust.

The country's long-term identity looks back to the older Empire of Karqašlu. Missions and the development diary describe it as an early human empire in Bulwar and the historical legitimacy Kumarkand invokes to challenge Sun Elf hegemony. But “we are the one true heir to the ancient empire” is first and foremost the country's political claim, not a neutral, established historical conclusion; its revival is a mission-tree future, not the reality of 1444. The offline English Wiki describes Kumarkand as a Zanite Akalate in Bulwar Proper and also records Varamhar as its overlord. Its notable-ruler panel, however, names Temenos II, conflicting with the current Mod's 1444 ruler, Serakh II of the Remmanu dynasty. This article follows the current Mod rather than combining the two character lists.

Sunriders, Rangers, and Three Faiths

Kumarkand's army has two distinctive calling cards. Sarraka Sunriders are cavalry with a magical tradition; an opening mission asks you to win the support of these now largely ceremonial riders for independence, and later missions can strengthen cavalry and battle mages. Kumarkandi Rangers, meanwhile, point toward special mercenaries and manpower support. This is not simply another Bulwari Sun Elf infantry empire: in war, you must consider how to use cavalry, mercenaries, and mages together. Missions also develop farmland, cities, and the elite, ultimately to restore the strength of a larger state.

Religion does not follow a single fixed line. Current events explicitly offer directions such as remaining in the New Sun Cult, adopting the Old Sun Cults, or embracing the Jadd; missions and events also use Karqašlu religious traditions to reshape political power. The goals, eligibility, and rewards of these routes should not be collapsed into a “standard sequence” that grants everything in one campaign. As the country grows from a small Akalate into a hegemon, events allow you to remain F30, form Surakeš (F52), or, if Jadd conditions are met, establish eligibility for a later Jadd Empire route. The script explicitly links the availability of F52's 52 related missions through was_tag = F30. These are optional branches—not an empire already present in 1444, nor one inevitable ending.

The Ancient Empire's Secrets and a Maritime Crisis

The revival route goes beyond reclaiming land. Missions send you to seek ancient relics, reorganize elite cavalry, develop farmland, and even investigate helmets able to resist magic. As the imperial dream grows, defenses along the Divenhal and a major ritual draw the player toward a crisis involving a creature from the deep. Current mission text explicitly presents the “Second Assault” as a later story with victory and defeat conditions; it does not establish that Kumarkand has already repelled it in history. The development diary offers a warning-like preview, while the present version's specific sequence is governed by local missions and events.

The v2.1 personality coordinates are Expansion 90/100 | Autocracy 76/100 | Magic ↔ Artifice 82/100 (100 = magic, 0 = artifice; theme intensity 68/100) | Pluralism 58/100. The v2.1 values assessment is Neutral (54/100), with a mixed trajectory. Protecting the homeland from external rule, developing farmland, and defending the coast against disaster serve the public good; the strong revanchism for an ancient empire, religious unification, and monarchical authority also constrain other groups' autonomy. War, monarchy, and religious propagation are not penalized in themselves; the evidence does not justify classifying the country directly as good or evil. Player posts praise the cavalry feel and religious-route choices, while also describing older mercenary organization and army-tradition requirements as frustrating bottlenecks; those reports should not be applied automatically to the current version.

The offline Wiki also records the “Tragedy of Samartal” outside Kumarkand in 1491: Old Sun Cult radicals attack a religious-political gathering. The entry contains editorial placeholder text, so it is only a flawed supplementary Wiki account. It neither proves that a player will encounter the same event nor replaces the outcomes defined by local scripts.

This country suits players who enjoy a long arc from “oppressed subject to independence to imperial revival,” mixed cavalry and mercenary armies, religious choices, and a later coastal crisis. It is a poor fit if you want a peaceful, short campaign, do not want to start as a subject, or expect to collect every mutually exclusive religious reward in one run.

National Ideas (Reference Appendix)

The following reproduces current national traditions, seven national ideas and ambition. Traditions apply on adoption, ideas unlock through investment, and ambition follows completion of all seven. Only national ideas are listed, not racial, governmental or mission bonuses; predecessor and successor sets do not stack. Idea descriptions can recall history or describe future ideals and do not automatically establish events before 1444.

Effect displays and units are inherited for source parity, not independently certified; uncertain percentages remain accompanied by script keys and raw values.

Kumarkand (F30) — Kumarkandi Ideas

Set ID: F30_ideas. Source: project-verified Mod script (public artifact omits local path and line offsets).

Applicability condition (source script):

    trigger = {
        tag = F30 #Kumarkand
    }

Kumarkandi Traditions

  • Military advisor cost: -25% (mil_advisor_cost; raw value -0.25).

  • Leader land shock: +1 (leader_land_shock; raw value 1).

1. Sarraka Auxiliaries

When Jaher arrived, he truly embodied Surael's awesomeness, strength, and power. We are reminded of him every time we bear witness to our Sarraka auxiliaries, the Sunriders: an elite force of elven mages, provided by our overlords in Varamhar, slinging powerful magic atop Kumarkand's finest warhorses. With their assistance, our cavalry can blast apart any foe.

(Of course, some of our citizens grumble they could do as good or better provided equal training...)

  • Cavalry shock: +25% (cavalry_shock; raw value 0.25).

2. Dryland Farming

Kumarkand defines, and is defined by, farming. Quite literally, our country's name means farmland. Since before we existed as a polity, we made our name in turning the region's arid land into lush verdure. And as long as the Suran flows, as long as Surael's sun shines bright over head, we shall continue to do so.

  • Development cost: -5% (development_cost; raw value -0.05).

  • global_manpower_modifier：+10% (global_manpower_modifier; raw value 0.1).

3. The Kumarkandi Draft Horse

Across Bulwar, the Kumarkandi are often derided as a stubborn and unyielding lot. But, if they ever met our horses, they would understand why. The beasts are twice as stubborn as even the most undiplomatic human, and it takes a people just as tough to control them.

But alas, they shall never quite learn this, for this well-worked creature can only be found in our own fields. And its rugged strength and indomitable spirit is what ensures our farmers grow the best and most produce in all Bulwar.

  • Production efficiency: +10% (production_efficiency; raw value 0.1).

4. The Rangers of Bulwar

Most Kumarkandi are content to spend their lives working the family farm, tending the fields of their fathers and their fathers' fathers. But every so often, one is born who is different, who seeks to wander different pastures under new skies.

Wherever they go, however, they carry with them the skills in-born to any Kumarkandi: loyalty, determination, fortitude, self-sufficiency. It is thus unsurprising many become talented rangers and adventurers (and similarly unsurprising when they offer their birth-country their services at reduced prices).

  • Mercenary Maintenance: -20% (merc_maintenance_modifier; raw value -0.2).

5. Abtu Khati

"Good abtu khati is made of quality refined flour, free of impurities such as husk and bran, with plenty of salt in it to break down its density. Let it ferment well, to create a good bread with airy and light texture. Knead the dough very well, let it rise, knead it again, divide it into portions, and wait until they rise. Ensure thin consistency, so it develops more bubbles as it bakes. Serve with dips, meats, and olive oil."

-An excerpt from The Book of Dishes, a famed 10th century text, describing the preparation of an equally famous Kumarkandi bread — the staple of every meal, and a faithful companion on every journey.

  • National Supply Limit Modifier: +25% (global_supply_limit_modifier; raw value 0.25).

6. Demos the Half Sun

Centuries ago, the Harpy Matriarchy treated Kumarkand as its personal hunting grounds, preying upon crops, livestock, and men with abandon. The fields grew desolate, ravaged by these savage reapers and abandoned by farmworkers. And then Demos arrived.

Adorned in bright bronze armor and a golden mask, he stood bright on the plains of Xharraranaz — an irresistible target. Over many months, with bow and spear and sword, he slew dozens of harpies who sought to claim him as their own. It was only when the Matriarch herself came, amidst a storm of wind and rain, that any of them could stand against him. And even she could not capture him; their duel ended in a mortal blow to Demos, the matriarch fluttering away with a wing sliced off (she would die of her wounds a few weeks later).

Afterwards, the local farmers hesitantly approached the hero's corpse, and unmasked him for the first time. They discovered that he was a half-elf, the only one ever known to walk the fields of Kumarkand. And while the stiff-necks in Bulwar decried this as abomination, we know the truth: he was chosen by Surael, and Demos the Half-Sun remains a legendary figure to this day.

  • Land morale recovery speed: +10% (recover_army_morale_speed; raw value 0.10).

7. The Discovery of the Ruins of Karqašlu

For centuries, the ruins of Karqašlu lay untouched, treated by the locals with a blend of superstition and fear. But the Varamhari lust for new magics led them to brush aside any such concerns and they mounted several expeditions into its depths. Though fruitless, they were only the first.

In 1601, Temenos Fula, the renowned local explorer, noticed an odd helmet buried under rubble. Adorning it, the artifact began to glow faintly, and immediately his magical items fell useless to his side. Whatever he had discovered, it seemed to grant a level of magical immunity to its wearer.

The Akal would claim the helmet (and its companions discovered in later expeditions) as Kumarkand's rightful property upon Fula's death, and they would become the core of an elite mage-resistant force within the state's armies. (Pay no heed to any mention of a strange voice entering one's mind when the helmet is worn, it is mere illusion and imagination).

  • shock_damage_received：-10% (shock_damage_received; raw value -0.1).

Kumarkandi Ambition

  • Aggressive expansion impact: -20% (ae_impact; raw value -0.2).

Surakeš (F52) — Surakeši Ideas

Set ID: F52_ideas. Source: project-verified Mod script (public artifact omits local path and line offsets).

Applicability condition (source script):

    trigger = {
        tag = F52 #Surakes
    }

Surakeši Traditions

  • Infantry combat ability: +10% (infantry_power; raw value 0.1).

  • global_manpower_modifier：+15% (global_manpower_modifier; raw value 0.15).

1. Ten Thousand Bazaars

It is said that Bulwar is the land of 10,000 bazaars. The abundance of markets, both great and small, means that the riches and artifacts of ages can be obtained almost as easily as the mundane goods of everyday life.

  • Trade efficiency: +15% (trade_efficiency; raw value 0.15).

2. Independent Judicial System

Bulwar has had a strong tradition of independent judges ever since ancient times. In those days, it was the Order of Judges that handled affairs of law and settled disputes between city-states. These days, that order has become more integrated into the government, but it still remains completely separate from the ruling power of Bulwar, capable of passing judgment without interference.

  • National unrest: -2 (global_unrest; raw value -2).

  • Republican tradition: +0.15 (republican_tradition; raw value 0.15).

  • Legitimacy: +0.5 (legitimacy; raw value 0.5).

  • Devotion: +0.5 (devotion; raw value 0.5).

  • Horde unity: +0.5 (horde_unity; raw value 0.5).

3. Between Cannor and Rahen

Bulwar is the oldest civilisation of man, but millennia of occupation has left it relatively poor. Instead it is situated between the wealthy lands of Rahen and Cannor, allowing the cities of Bulwar to flourish from the trade routes running through their lands. Throughout the years, the Bulwari developed strong foreign trading relations, not just with Rahen and Cannor, but also with the rest of Haless, with the Serpentspine and with Sarhal.

  • Global trade power: +20% (global_trade_power; raw value 0.2).

4. Divenhal Domination

Bulwari trade is heavily reliant on the Divenhal. Cities like Brasan, Anzabad, Re-Uyel and Aqatbar all have ports and heavy trading connections with the cities of northern Sarhal and southern Cannor. To fully capitalize on these trading connections, a project has begun to build a great many galleys to protect those trade routes and to allow Bulwar to project its power over all coasts of the Divenhal.

  • Galley construction cost: -25% (galley_cost; raw value -0.25).

  • Galley Combat Ability: +20% (galley_power; raw value 0.2).

5. Freedom from Gnoll and Elf

Bulwar had never been united under humans. The disparate city-states were first dominated by genies, then gnolls, then sun elves. For the first time Bulwar is united under human rule, a union of city-states ruled by one of their own, instead of a foreign power.

  • Army morale: +10% (land_morale; raw value 0.1).

6. The Flooding of the Suran

The Suran, the most important river of Bulwar, is subject to seasonal flooding. In times of old, the city-states of Bulwar made use of that flooding for the irrigation of their fields, but it was never a united effort. These days, the irrigation system is managed centrally, and the people of Bulwar have much more control over the flooding of the great river. This allows for vast quantities of food to be produced, all feeding into a growing population.

  • Development cost: -20% (development_cost; raw value -0.2).

7. The Magi of Bulwar

While often suppressed and rarely noticed, Bulwar is a land of ancient knowledge. While genies dominated their human subjects, some of those subjects also learned the secrets of their overlords. This tradition was later developed and expanded and left Bulwar as a land of powerful mages. While under gnollish rule, this art was mostly lost, and it didn't regain much of its former glory while under the sun elves. In Dartaxâgerdim, the old art was revived and an arcane society rose to prominence and now flourishes all over Bulwar.

  • All power costs: -2.5% (all_power_cost; raw value -0.025).

Surakeši Ambition

  • Land fire damage: +10% (fire_damage; raw value 0.1).

Jadd Empire (F51) — Jadd Empire Ideas

Set ID: F51_ideas. Source: project-verified Mod script (public artifact omits local path and line offsets).

Applicability condition (source script):

    trigger = {
        OR = {
            tag = F51 #Jadd Empire
            tag = F99 #Jadd Empire Civil War
        }
    }

Jadd Empire Traditions

  • Cavalry combat ability: +20% (cavalry_power; raw value 0.2).

  • Missionary strength: +2% (global_missionary_strength; raw value 0.02).

1. Expand the Legions

When the Legions adopted the Jadd, they also opened up their ranks to a much greater variety of people and races. While this was initially disruptive and led to a decrease in discipline and organization, it also had as an immediate effect that it greatly increased the manpower pool the state could draw from. This allowed the Jadd Empire to pull on greater amounts of men than their neighbours.

  • Manpower from true faith provinces: +20% (manpower_in_true_faith_provinces; raw value 0.2).

2. Native Bureaucrats

All within the Jadd are equal and it would not do to suppress any cultures or races. So the Jadd Empire followed a practice of leaving local administrations intact to cause minimal disruption. Where feudal systems existed, the local lords needed to report to the imperial governor, but the rest was left intact. The same occurred with more modern administrations. Only in very tribal systems with no clear power structure was order brought by restructuring the local systems, but local chiefs still stayed in power. Of course all of this was if they did not revolt. This system allowed large areas to be swiftly integrated and reduced the need for forming new local administrations.

  • Governing Capacity Modifier: +20% (governing_capacity_modifier; raw value 0.2).

3. Spread the Faith

At the heart of the Jadd Empire stood the faith of the Jadd. While proclaiming the empire had given the faith a clear home and base to rally around, the Jadd was not an isolationist religion. Its core tenet was the banishment of the dark, so the Empire ever sought to expand its borders and to spread the faith to new lands. It could not rest until the darkness was banished from all lands.

  • War score cost against other religions: -20% (warscore_cost_vs_other_religion; raw value -0.2).

4. Restructure the Legions

The old Phoenix Legions underwent great changes since the Sun Elves first landed on shores of Bulwar. The experience they gained while campaigning through Sarhal and Haless made them strong. The adaptation to the eastern Salahad made them crafty. The next reform would leave them changed to an even greater degree. The mixing of different races into the army would have made them unrecognisable to Jaher's army. However the experience and drill of their veterans forged these different groups into one force, now also driven by a common purpose: To defend and to spread the Light of the Jadd.

  • Discipline: +5% (discipline; raw value 0.05).

5. Rebuild the Golden Highway

The Golden Highway of Jaher was the greatest infrastructure project the world had seen until that point. So great that the following generations could not keep up with its maintenance. Until the Jadd Empire stepped in and reconnected the ancient Bulwari lands with its core lands around the Mountain of Clear Sight. A new highway was constructed in the place of the old one, recreating the connection between Haless and Bulwar. Its control gave the Jadd greater power over its trade and also allowed swift movement of troops from one end of the empire to another.

  • Trade efficiency: +10% (trade_efficiency; raw value 0.1).

  • Movement speed: +15% (movement_speed; raw value 0.15).

6. Increase Lightbringer Jurisdiction

The order of Lightbringers was a class of warriors, scribes, rhetoricians and clerics that had as a task to safeguard the light within the state. Their tasks mainly revolved around seeking out heathens and heretics and either making them see the light, or bringing them to trial. In the days of the Jadd Empire their powers were extended to bypass the courts and to instantly deal with anyone who did not comply with the tenets of the faith. This would lead to occasional riots and more than one instance of the burning of innocents, but it did quicken the spread of the faith within the Empire.

  • True faith tolerance: +1 (tolerance_own; raw value 1).

  • Harsh treatment cost: -25% (harsh_treatment_cost; raw value -0.25).

7. The True Successors of Surael

Since time immemorial the central question of the Bulwari religion has been how the world responds to the death or return of Surael. The Sun Cult proclaimed Jaher to be the god's reincarnation, and when he died the Sun Elves were appointed as the successors. Jaddar claimed that all people who follow the truth would be Surael's successors. In turn those who follow the Jadd see their leader as the Divine Herald and the voice of the Sun God.

  • Army morale: +10% (land_morale; raw value 0.1).

  • Yearly absolutism: +1 (yearly_absolutism; raw value 1).

Jadd Empire Ambition

  • Administrative efficiency: +5% (administrative_efficiency; raw value 0.05).
